title: Compatible local quotient charts without a covering hypothesis
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], L an invertible X-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and S its graded section ring [def-sc-invertible-section-ring]. Let I be an arbitrary index type. For each i let d_i > 0, s_i a homogeneous section of degree d_i, and U_i an open whose underlying set is the nonvanishing locus of s_i [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. The U_i need not cover X. There exist morphisms g_i:U_i -> Proj(S) [def-pc-proj] which agree on each pairwise intersection. For every i, homogeneous t of any positive degree e, n >= 0, and homogeneous xi of degree ne, let W_i,t be the ambient image in X of g_i^{-1}(D_+(t)). Under the identification O_{U_i}(g_i^{-1}(D_+(t))) = O_X(W_i,t), the pullback by g_i of xi/t^n, multiplied by the restriction of t^n to W_i,t, equals the restriction of xi to W_i,t. This is only local data; there is no assertion of a morphism from X.

proof.text: For each index i apply the single quotient chart theorem to the given positive-degree section and its prescribed nonvanishing open. Choice gives a dependent family g_i, with the homogeneous fraction equations for every i. This choice takes place only in the proof of an existential theorem; it introduces no definition of arbitrarily chosen data.

proof.text: For every i,j apply the overlap comparison theorem to g_i and g_j with their fraction equations. It yields precisely the two composites from U_i intersect U_j in the conclusion. Pair these equations with the already chosen family fraction equations. There is no assumption that the opens cover X, and this assembly also works for an empty index type.
